messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: post hoc power analysis in CFA
parts:
Without knowing what you're interested in power for (parameter estimates? model fit?) it is hard to give a precise answer. If you want to use a Monte Carlo power analysis, look into the simsem package (which can use a lavaan object as input). Check out example 7 in the vignettes at simsem.org.

Alex

On 05/09/2014 07:25 PM, Ivan Jacob Pesigan wrote:
> Correct me if I am wrong, for the model fit I will have to compare the
> fit indices produced from my data and the simulated fit indices cutoff
> points right? I used the MLR estimator do I compare the usual estimates
> or the robust estimates with the cutoffs? The obtained fit indices
> should be greater that the cutoffs right at a particular alpha level to
> be able to say that there is adequate power?

I would hesitate to use the term 'power' for fit indices that have no
parametric distribution. But that does not mean that the simulated
'distribution' of these fit indices may not be informative.

Yves.
